title: Echeloned Release Policy DSL and Safety Net for Model Variants
creator: Aisha Morgan
description:
Problem: Current rollout primitives are either too coarse (single-step traffic swaps) or too rigid (fixed canary percentages), making it hard for product teams to express nuanced staged releases for model variants. We need a compact, composable DSL that operators and platform integrators can use to describe multi-stage traffic schedules, cohort targeting, shadow probes, A/B branches, and automated rollback guardrails tied to observed telemetry.

Goals:
- Define a human-readable policy DSL that can be validated and compiled to routing rules.
- Support: staged weights, time-or-metric-driven steps, cohort scoping, shadow traffic, and A/B forks.
- Express guardrails: metric thresholds (latency, p95, error-rate, quality regressions), evaluation windows, and escalation actions (pause, rollback, escalate to on-call).
- Make policies first-class in the Console (preview, dry-run, safety checks) and integrate with telemetry and alerting for auto-rollback.

Constraints & non-goals:
- Not a full feature flag system — focus on model-serving traffic split semantics.
- We will compile DSL to existing routing primitives; avoid changes that require sharding routing tables.
- Backward compatibility: existing canary configs should continue to work; provide a migration path.
rollout_policy_snippet:
# Example DSL (YAML-style)
policy_name: echeloned_variant_rollout
description: staged release for text-generation-v2 -> text-generation-v2-quant
selectors:
  - service: api.text.generate
  - model: text-generation-v2
steps:
  - id: step-1
    when: elapsed(5m) or metric(p95_latency) < 250ms
    weight: 5%
    cohorts:
      - global
  - id: step-2
    when: elapsed(30m) and metric(quality.delta) >= -0.01
    weight: 20%
    cohorts:
      - mobile-users
      - beta-customers
  - id: step-3
    when: manual_approve
    weight: 100%
shadow_probe:
  enabled: true
  sample: 2%
  compare_with: baseline
guardrails:
  - metric: error_rate
    window: 10m
    threshold: 1.0%
    action: rollback
  - metric: p95_latency
    window: 5m
    threshold: 500ms
    action: pause_and_notify
rollback_policy:
  max_consecutive_failures: 2
  rollback_window: 30m
  notify: ["oncall-sre", "owner-team"]
acceptance_criteria: DSL syntax documented and linter implemented (schema + CLI validator)
Policy compiler converts DSL into existing routing rules and unit tests cover compilation cases
Console UI renders policy preview and simulates traffic split for historical request traces
Telemetry hooks emit per-step metrics (rate, latency, quality delta) and trigger configured guardrail actions
Auto-rollback works in a staging environment with a configurable cooldown and notification flow
infra_changes: routing-layer: add staged weight tokens and evaluation-time checks
control-plane: policy compiler service + validation endpoints
console: policy authoring + dry-run + step visualizer
telemetry: per-policy step telemetry and SLI aggregation windows
alerting: map DSL guardrails to alert rules and PagerDuty integration
estimated_risks: Complex guardrails could produce noisy rollbacks if metrics are unstable; mitigated by configurable windows and hysteresis.
Policy compiler bugs could mis-route traffic — plan: exhaustive unit/e2e tests and shadow rollout before enabling auto-apply.
UI confusion for non-technical users — provide templates and simplified preset policies for common patterns.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Aisha Morgan: Created ticket after staging postmortem showed manual rollouts caused regression regressions. Initial draft DSL attached.

2025-02-18 - Daniel Park: Spike complete — implemented prototype compiler that emits routing rules and a simple simulator. Found an edge-case where cohort scoping intersects with routing cache invalidation; opened ENG-21505 to track cache invalidation behavior.

2025-02-21 - Priya Shah (SRE): Reviewed guardrail actions. Requested 'pause_and_notify' action to include automatic shadow-probing for 10 minutes before rollback. Asked for explicit cooldowns on rollback to avoid flapping.
2025-02-25 - Design review (Liam Chen): Console visualization mockups look good; recommended adding 'explain' mode that shows why a step would/ wouldn't progress based on recent metrics.
2025-03-01 - Daniel Park: Implemented linter + CI check; added test harness to run policy dry-runs against historical traces (see PR 9234). Working on integrating per-step telemetry tags.

2025-03-05 - Aisha Morgan: Decision: default policy preset 'safe-staged' will include 3 steps (5%, 25%, 100%), 30m evaluation windows, and auto-rollback on >1% error-rate delta. Need follow-up for runbook updates and oncall playbook (task queued).
next_steps: Complete console dry-run UI and connect to simulation backend (owner: Design + Frontend)
Implement guardrail hysteresis and cooldown config in compiler runtime (owner: Backend)
Add migration tool to convert existing simple canaries to DSL wrappers (owner: Ops)
Schedule SRE tabletop runbook review and PD mapping (owner: SRE)
notes: This ticket intentionally keeps the DSL surface area small to accelerate adoption. Advanced features (percentile-based cohorting, multi-metric composite guards) are planned in a follow-up epic.
Keep operator-facing language explicit: 'pause', 'rollback', 'notify', 'probe'. Avoid jargon in console UX.
